t.E952.agn: In 2000 the EU Scientific Committee on Food (SCF) set the ADI at 7 mg/kg body weight, expressed as cyclamic acid, based on the effect of cyclohexylamine on the testes in rats and the highest conversion rate observed in humans (the previous temporary value was 11 mg/kg). EFSA's re-evaluation started in 2026 and is expected to be completed in June 2027.
t.E952.body: Cyclamate is not completely absorbed; in some people, the unabsorbed portion is converted to cyclohexylamine at variable rates by bacteria in the large intestine.
t.E952.eff.0.t: In some people, gut bacteria convert cyclamate to cyclohexylamine; this substance affected the testes in rats, and the daily limit is based on this finding
t.E952.eff.0.w: People who convert cyclamate (the rate varies from person to person)
t.E952.eval: Not authorised in food in the USA since 1969 (21 CFR 189.135). Authorised in the EU; in 2000 the SCF set the acceptable daily intake at 7 mg/kg, and EFSA's re-evaluation is ongoing.
t.E952.found.1: Energy-reduced or no-added-sugar flavoured fermented milk products
t.E952.prod: A sweetener produced chemically by sulphonation of cyclohexylamine.
t.E952.regx.0: Revised opinion; ADI 0–7 mg/kg body weight (as cyclamic acid). Following this opinion, maximum use levels in the EU were lowered (2003/115/EC).
t.E952.regx.1: Re-evaluation ongoing; expected to be completed in June 2027.
t.E952.regx.2: On the EU list of authorised additives; in most food categories authorised only in energy-reduced or no-added-sugar products.
t.E952.summary: A synthetic sweetener about 30-50 times sweeter than sugar. Used in diet drinks and table-top sweeteners.
t.E952.what: A calorie-free synthetic sweetener about 30–40 times sweeter than sugar.
t.agency.FDA_banned_1970: Its use in food was banned in the USA.
t.kaynak.dd6dfbbb0f: European Commission Scientific Committee on Food (SCF)
